LaTeX source and verification code for the paper *Weak-Type Endpoint Bounds for Bochner–Riesz Means in Every Dimension* by Deep Bhattacharjee (57 pages).

At the critical index the Bochner–Riesz means in every dimension n ≥ 2 are of weak type (p,p) for 1 < p < 2n/(n+1), uniformly in the radius, and converge in weak L^p (Theorem A); they have sparse bounds on the critical side of the Beltran–Roos–Seeger trapezoid, sharp except at its corner (Theorem B), and weighted weak-type bounds for every A_1 weight with a range of p governed by its reverse Hölder exponent, end point included (Theorem C and Section 10). For n ≥ 3 these follow from OpenAI's preprint *Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation* (25 October 2026) through the conditional theorems of Tao and of Beltran, Roos and Seeger; the paper reproduces OpenAI's argument and the ε-removal of Beltran, Roos and Seeger in full, with credit.

Changes since v1.0.0: Theorem B is stated in its nontrivial range q < p' (Lemma 9.2 shows that sparse forms are infinite when 1/p + 1/q ≤ 1); the introduction credits the conditional statements of Tao and of Beltran, Roos and Seeger; the corner and the top side at λ = (n−1)/(2n+2) are attributed to Beltran, Roos and Seeger; Section 10 proves that the weighted range includes its right end point, with explicit constants and a range for A_1 weights alone; Section 11 explains why the corner of the trapezoid is out of reach of these methods.

Attached: the compiled paper, the TeX sources as a zip, and an arXiv tarball. The check program (27 checks) and the Lean 4 file (18 theorems, standard axioms only) are in the repository.
